To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PFC, but not the VIP, exhibits increased numerosity coding after numerosity training, and that the increased numerosity coding is evidenced by increased differentiation of numerosity in the population of neurons as well as increased number selectivity by individual neurons.
the representation of numerosity changes in the prefrontal cortex (PFA) after learning, but not in the posterior parietal ventral intrapariental area (VIP).
the PFC and VIP encode number in a similar fashion, but that PFC neurons, unlike VIP neurons, show enhanced number representations when monkeys learn a numerical task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the representation of quantity in the brain depends on the task demands.
the neural representation of numerical quantity.
the question of how the brain represents quantity, and how the brain represents number.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PFC is more sensitive to behavioral relevance than the posterior parietal area.
PFC and VIP are both involved in numerosity processing, but that the PFC is involved in a more flexible and dynamic fashion, whereas the VIP is more involved in a more rigid and invariant fashion.
quantity is encoded in the PFC as a function of behavioral relevance, but is encoded in VIP as a function of quantity itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PFC and VIP encode quantity differently: PFC encodes quantity in relation to task demands whereas VIP encodes it as a perceptual attribute.

the PFC and VIP have distinct roles in quantity processing: the PFC is involved in the active discrimination of numerical magnitude, whereas the VIP is involved in the passive perception of numerical magnitude.
quantity is represented in the PFC, but not in the VIP, when it is relevant for a behavioral task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the representation of quantity can be modulated by behavioral context.

the prefrontal cortex, but not the posterior parietal, is involved in quantity discrimination and that the prefrontum may play a key role in the representation of numerosity as a quantity that is relevant for the organism's behavior.
the prefrontal cortex and the ventral intrapartietal cortex have differential roles in the representation of quantity.
